title: fix: resume persisted requests when transcript metadata advances
body:
## What Problem This Solves

A persisted user request can fail during initial replay preparation when another writer appends transcript metadata between selection and admission. The user then has to resend an unchanged request.

## User Impact

A benign transcript advance now gets one fresh preparation and admission attempt. A replaced user, completed turn, lost writer claim, or revoked authority still refuses replay. There are no runtime configuration or schema changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The final-consumption path already retried once after #181473, but initial preparation used the same read owner without that recovery. Move the existing bounded retry into the shared owner, retain the original entry ID and generation across refresh, and record consumption before calling the consumer. This avoids a second retry layer and preserves exactly-once user-turn consumption.

Current readers throw `SessionTranscriptReadFenceError` for the reproduced version mismatch before returning context-validation facts. The owner handles that existing form and work-start invalidation without changing source, writer, or authority validation.

## Evidence

The new real-SQLite regression is red on base `71ee55620d0786d4078dfa41c3527488c4a7cad4`: a metadata append between selection and admission rejects initial preparation. The fix refreshes once, admits once, and retains one user message. Newer-user and repeated-advance cases still reject. All 80 focused/session/replay sibling cases pass, plus all 16 required prompt-prefix stability cases (96 total).

The complete initial `pnpm check:changed --staged --timed` run passed, as did `pnpm deadcode:unused-files`. After the CI repair, changed-file checks ran again; the nullable-generation type error was fixed and all three affected type graphs passed on rerun. Every remaining changed-file gate passed; the original failed run and targeted passing reruns are retained as evidence. Independent Codex autoreview at P0–P2 is scoped-clean on the final five-file candidate against base `71ee55620d0786d4078dfa41c3527488c4a7cad4`. No Control UI import boundary changes. The repaired 70-case focused/sibling run took 110.92 seconds, and the 10-case recovery/persistence run took 40.96 seconds. Initial CI run 44407917446 caught a PR-caused session-identity ratchet failure from a duplicated anchor guard. The repair shares the existing final guard with initial preparation and passes the ratchet; no inherited-failure waiver is used. Local typechecking caught a nullable-generation annotation, now corrected with all three affected type graphs passing. The complete [dispatched CI run 44412352144](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44412352144) passed on final head `e7eab8d0c898d0a6c23a8c48d916873d916ab467`. The normal [ready-for-review CI run 44414749132](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44414749132) also passed on that exact head. ClawSweeper re-review on this exact head has zero open items and no findings.

The committed benchmark uses an offline synthetic 5,000-session database and a 62,000-file workspace. Measurement acceptance was set before the comparison: two A/A controls and five interleaved A/B process pairs for steady and raced admission, with timing and sampled-allocation passes separated. Unchanged-path cost must stay within control variation; raced admission must succeed exactly once after one refresh. Recovery necessarily does more work than the baseline's failed request, so it is not presented as a latency speedup. The generated agent database is 37,792,735,232 bytes (35.20 GiB), with 200,640 transcript messages and 1.116 GB of workspace file contents. Timing and allocation passes are complete. Each arm has 100 warm observations across five interleaved process pairs, plus separately reported first-use samples.

| Case | Wall median / p95 (ms), before → after | Process CPU median (ms) | Main-thread CPU median (ms) | Sampled main-thread allocation median (MB) | Admitted turns |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Steady | 11.93 / 13.86 → 11.76 / 14.16 | 28.72 → 27.78 | 4.36 → 4.33 | 1.418 → 1.400 | 100/100 → 100/100 |
| Concurrent append | 14.74 / 18.51 → 24.06 / 31.55 | 31.91 → 43.54 | 5.09 → 7.86 | 1.650 → 2.842 | 0/100 → 100/100 |

Steady A/A wall medians were 14.05 and 11.88 ms; sampled-allocation control medians were 1.397 and 1.406 MB. Steady cost remains within control variation. Race recovery adds 9.32 ms median wall time and 1.192 MB sampled main-thread allocation relative to failure, with exactly one refresh and no duplicate user message. First-use wall medians: steady 351.98 → 350.06 ms; race 349.56 → 366.17 ms. Process CPU includes workers; allocation sampling covers the main thread only. A separate 100-iteration CPU profile was inspected; startup/esbuild and forced GC dominate whole-process samples and are excluded from the timed owner windows. No Linux/btrfs, live Gateway, or external-provider equivalence is claimed.

Production delta: +8 lines for selection identity and callback-consumption ownership, with the old final-only retry deleted. The regression adds 58 lines; the standalone benchmark is supporting proof.
